Revision No. 492 of 2003 Arun Kumar Mahatha S/o Late Kedar Nath Mahtha, resident of village - Bijulia, P.S. Chas (M.), District-Bokaro .... Petitioner Versus The State of Jharkhand .... Opposite party --- Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice Anubha Rawat Choudhary --- For the Petitioner : Mr. Sanjay Kumar, Advocate For the State : Mr. Abhay Kumar Tiwari, A.P.P.
texts.facts: Opposite ... on 13 September, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20295085/ 1 5. Findings of the Court 8. The case of the prosecution in brief is that on 9.11.1989, the food inspector, Chas alongwith licence supervisor and health supervisor had visited the food grain shop of the petitioner, where the petitioner was present and the shop was also open. On demand by the food inspector, the petitioner had produced his licence for running food grains shop, which was valid only till 31.03.1986. Therefore, the food inspector prepared the prosecution report and also obtained the signature of his other two aforesaid associates on the prosecution report. Thereafter the food inspector sent the prosecution report for sanction for prosecution to the local health authority and after receipt of the sanction order, the report was filed and the case was instituted, in which cognizance was taken. The charge was framed against the petitioner in the aforesaid provision of Prevention of Food Arun Kumar Mahatha S/O Late Kedar Nath ... vs The State Of Jharkhand .... Opposite ... on 13 September, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20295085/ 2 Adulteration Act, 1954, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 9. The prosecution examined altogether three witnesses. P.W.- 1 is the food inspector, P.W.-2 is the health supervisor and P.W.-3 is the licensing supervisor. All these three persons had jointly visited the place of occurrence. 10. As per the evidence of PW-1, food inspector, on 9.11.89 at about 10 am, he along with PW-2 and PW-3 had visited the food grain shop of the petitioner, where he found the petitioner and the shop was open and when he asked for license of the shop, the petitioner had produced the license, which was valid till 31.03.1986. PW-1 further stated that on being asked, the petitioner had told him that he will get his license renewed. Thereafter, PW - 1 prepared the prosecution report (Ext.-1), on which he obtained the signatures of the other two associates, i.e. PW-2 and PW-3 and sent the proposal for sanction to local health authority and local health authority being satisfied given the sanctioned order, which was exhibited as Ext. 2. 11. The evidence of PW-2 has been recorded in the trial court judgment, wherein, it has been recorded that PW - 2 stated that on the date and time of occurrence, he went alongwith PW- 1 and PW - 3 and visited the food grain shop of the petitioner, where they found that the shop of the petitioner was opened and sell was going on. He further stated that PW-1 had demanded the licence of the shop of the petitioner, which was found to be valid till 31.3.86 and after 31.3.86 and the petitioner was running the food grain shop without any licence on the date of inspection.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the impugned judgments convicting the petitioner for offence under Section 16 (1) (a) (ii) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is ex facie perverse. He submitted that as per the allegation, the petitioner, in spite of expiry of license, was running the shop of food grains. Learned counsel submitted that no food grain was seized from the shop and no independent witness has been examined to support the prosecution case. He also submitted that no weighing machine or weight or balance etc. has been seized from the alleged shop. He submitted that no food grain has been recovered even from the possession of any buyer or any other person. He submitted that the petitioner has been convicted only on the basis of prosecution report which was supported by three witnesses who are official witnesses. The learned counsel submitted that the prosecution has not been able to prove the case beyond all reasonable doubt. He submitted that in absence of any food grain or any article having been seized from the alleged place of occurrence i.e. shop of the petitioner, no case of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act for the alleged offence is made out against the petitioner in the present case. 6. Learned counsel has also submitted that there is material contradiction so far as P.W.-2 is concerned, who had stated in his deposition that it was food grain shop of another person namely, Arjun Mahatha, which was raided, and said Arjun Mahatha was already acquitted by the court of Sub- Judicial Magistrate, Bokaro in another case i.e. Prevention of Food Adulteration Act Case No.9 of 1990. Learned counsel submitted that Arjun Mahatha has nothing to do with the shop of the petitioner and accordingly, P.W.-2 has in fact not supported the case of the prosecution by naming Arjun Mahatha whose shop was raided. Arguments on behalf of the State 7. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the opposite party- State, on the other hand, has submitted that there are concurrent findings recorded by the learned courts below and it has come in evidence that the petitioner was found running his shop, although his license had expired. However, he does not dispute the fact that no recovery whatsoever was made from the shop of the petitioner including recovery of any food grains or any balance, weighing machine and weight etc. for measurement of food grain and admittedly, no independent witness has been examined and the prosecution witness have not even disclosed the name of any independent person, who was said to be present at the place and time of occurrence. The specific defence of the petitioner was that he has not committed any offence and he has been falsely implicated. The further defence was that after the expiry of period of license, the petitioner closed his shop and on the day of alleged occurrence also, the shop of the petitioner was closed. It has been specifically argued by learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner that the learned trial court has wrongly recorded the evidence of PW - 2 in para - 7 of the Judgment that he had stated that he had visited the food grain shop of the petitioner along with PW - 1 and PW - 3, rather PW - 2 had stated that he had visited the food grain shop of another person including Arjun Mahatha, in connection with which another case was instituted.
